changes: Texas is the new risk: Beacon Point's baseload designation depends on a state audit, with results expected 10 December and final 17 December; management anticipates an unconditional classification, with 700 MW energization in 1Q27.
Phase 2 financing has no date: it follows the December result. The Phase 2 lease was extended from 15 to 17 years to help offset potentially higher financing costs.
The buyback was walked back in tone: 'we do not plan to continue to buy aggressively' and no revolver for buybacks, after $250mn at about $74.88 a share against a $48.94 close on 4 November.
Free parent bitcoin is thinner than it looked: 1,361 unencumbered BTC at 1 November (about $107mn at $78,265) against about 6,200 parent BTC derived in our pre-call note.

Management says the current build approach, 'NASA rocket programs', will not work at multi-gigawatt scale; existing projects stay on plan and design efficiency should offset rising cost, with no figure.

'Recourse to the parent' transcript line reads oddly and is not relied on. Derived numbers computed in Python ($74.88, 13%, $107mn). BTC price $78,265 from 24/7 Wall St (one source). Corrections applied: analyst counts, equity wording, 949 MW in 2Q (597 before July). Prices from StockAnalysis, intraday 5 November. No bond quote. Scorecard and themes written.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Hut 8 as the best-financed listed AI landlord (949 MW on 15- to 17-year triple-net leases, $7.5bn of non-recourse investment-grade bonds), and doubt sector funding and how Beacon Point Phase 2 gets paid for.
headline: The consensus view should turn more cautious on funding and on Texas, though not on contracts: project bonds and construction hold, but Phase 2 waits on a December state decision, free parent liquidity is smaller after the buyback, and the stock's 23% fall on 4 November says the market has already moved.
kona: Hut 8 gave more term, not more rent, to help the bond math: a 15 to 17 year lease is a tool Kona can ask for at small scale. It is also buying energized West Texas sites from a bankruptcy process at up to about $0.78mn per utility MW, a floor for bare energized power, and on the call it said capital scarcity is producing such assets. The Texas audit shows how a state decision can hold up an investment-grade financing; Kona should list Neuquen and national permits as conditions precedent lenders will price, and line up lenders before signing.
monitor: 17 December Texas result and any 1Q27 energization change.
Phase 2 financing: size, loan-to-cost, coupon, and any parent equity.
Parent liquidity against the revolver test from 1Q27, and retirement of the $200mn FalconX loan before April 2027.

sections.body: Emphasized more: discipline, the December Texas calendar, changing the build template, cash ('we believe that cash will be king'), Louisiana. Emphasized less or dropped: Phase 2 financing timing, promised for 'the coming weeks' in August; the buyback as a priority; Texas compared with Louisiana was not made explicit. KPIs more important: free parent liquidity; capex against dates. Less: GAAP EPS, driven by $413.8mn bitcoin gain. Risks up: Texas, Phase 2, parent liquidity. Down: River Bend construction. sections.body: 5 signals: 17 December Texas result; Phase 2 financing; revolver draws; free BTC; new lease. Key risks building: Texas; parent cushion; concentration.
